cohort: The study included mothers and their infants, consisting of hospital-born (vaginal/cesarean) and home-born (vaginal) infants.
finding: Delivery setting, breastfeeding duration, and other lifestyle preferences collectively shape vertical microbiota transmission, impacting infant gut colonization during early life.
mod_finding: Delivery mode primarily explains initial microbiota compositional differences, while place of birth impacts transmission timing, being early in homebirths and delayed in cesarean deliveries, and transmission patterns vary across species and birth groups.
followup_time: During the first year of life
